subject: Linguistics
title: Language in Education
description: A quick win: understand Language in Education.

hook.text: A child who speaks perfect Navajo at home is told at school that only English counts.

buildup.text: Schools typically enforce one standard language—marginalizing students who speak other varieties.

discovery.text: Research shows children learn better when their home language is valued, not suppressed.

twist.text: Bilingual education programs improve outcomes in both languages—not just the home language.

climax.text: Language-in-education policies shape which children succeed and which are disadvantaged.

punchline.text: A school's language policy is its hidden curriculum.

quiz.question: What does research show about valuing home languages in school?
options: Children learn better when home language is valued
